newsitem.title: UK: GDR REPORT - Indian GDRs follow locals lower.
newsitem.headline: GDR REPORT - Indian GDRs follow locals lower.

text.p: Indian global depositary receipts (GDRs) followed the local market lower in depressed trade.
"It really is very quiet: you can say all you like about this market being cheap but the fund managers are looking at it and saying "it is going to go nowehere before the year end'," said a trader.

The James Capel Indian GDR Index 0.73 points, or 1.06 percent, to 68.78 points, a premium of 13.16 percent over the local market after the Bombay Stock Exchange 30 share index fell 15.69 points, 0.47 percent, to 3,307.20.
Premiums for GDRs have come up from parity to over 10 percent.
"These are good companies and are fundamentally cheap but after the market went up two percent in one day last week and down two the following day, it became a bit hopeless," said the trader.

Elsewhere in Asia, the Capel Taiwan Index fell 0.31 points, 0.35 percent, to 88.21 points, a premium of 3.31 percent over the local market after the Taiwan Weighted Index closed down 36.11 at 6,453.98.

After the market closed, the central bank and finance ministry said they would raise the ceiling on foreign ownership of Taiwan stock-market equity to 25 percent from 20 percent and the ceiling in any single listed company was being raised to 10 percent from 7.5 percent.
The liberalisation will take effect before the end of this year.
The Capel Korea Index rose 1.35 points, 2.09 percent, to 65.85 points, a premium of 26.44 percent over the local market after the composite stock index closed up 0.83 point to a provisional 769.20.
Korea too is increasing foreign shareholderings, to 20 percent from 18 percent, from October 1.
